summary: World's second-largest startup ecosystem, centred on Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou, strong in AI, EVs, hardware, robotics and biotech. Many exits via STAR Market and Hong Kong listings. USD-fund activity has fallen since 2022 and RMB state-guided funds now dominate.
startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; founders use Z work, M business or R talent visas; some free-trade zones run talent schemes), https://en.nia.gov.cn
company_setup: Wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company registered with SAMR. Usually needs a local registered address and in-person or agent filings, so remote setup in practice goes through an agent. Under the 2024 Company Law, registered capital must be paid within 5 years. Takes about 1-3 months.

grants.name: National Key R&D Program
grants.eligibility: Companies and institutions in priority tech fields, competitive calls
grants.deadline: annual (calls usually late in the year)

grants.name: Specialized, Refined, Distinctive and Innovative SMEs (Little Giants)
grants.agency: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
grants.eligibility: Tech SMEs certified at provincial or national level

grants.name: Shenzhen science and technology funding (startup and R&D subsidies)
grants.agency: Shenzhen Science, Technology and Innovation Commission

grants.name: Shanghai Science and Technology Innovation Action Plan
grants.agency: Science and Technology Commission of Shanghai Municipality (STCSM)

grants.name: Beijing science and technology programs (incl. Zhongguancun support)
grants.agency: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

grants.name: National Natural Science Foundation grants
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Chinese institutions, useful for university spin-outs

accelerators.name: InnoSpace (Inno Angels)
accelerators.investment: seed investment via Inno Angel Fund

accelerators.name: Plug and Play China
accelerators.investment: no equity required for corporate programs

accelerators.name: Huawei Cloud Startup Program
accelerators.investment: cloud credits and go-to-market support, no equity

resources.name: Zero2IPO
resources.note: VC and PE data and events

notes: As of Oct 2026, US outbound investment rules restrict US LPs and investors in AI, semiconductors and quantum, so most new money is RMB and state-guided. Government calls are mostly Chinese-only and published per city or district. Fund check sizes are rarely published. Web search was exhausted during research, so several entities were verified by direct site checks only.

summary: Asia's second-largest ecosystem by VC volume, centred on Tokyo, with Osaka, Kyoto and Fukuoka as secondary hubs. Strong deep tech, B2B SaaS and university spin-outs, backed by the government's 5-Year Startup Development Plan. Most exits are IPOs on TSE Growth, and M&A is rising.
startup_visa: Startup Visa (Designated Activities No.44) through certified local governments such as Tokyo: one year, extendable to about two years, then a switch to Business Manager, which since Oct 2025 needs JPY 30M capital and one full-time staff member. https://www.investtokyo.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jp/oursupports/bdc-tokyo/startupvisa.html
company_setup: Kabushiki Kaisha (KK) or Godo Kaisha (GK). A foreigner can incorporate through a judicial scrivener without being resident, but a Japanese bank account and address are practical hurdles. Takes about 2-4 weeks. The Tokyo One-Stop Center helps with filings.

grants.name: Deep-Tech Startup Support Fund: International Joint R&D (FY2026)
grants.eligibility: Unlisted Japanese SMEs under 10 yrs with a foreign partner in an eligible country

grants.name: GX_UPP: Business development support for GX deep-tech startups (3rd call)
grants.amount: up to JPY 5bn (1/2 subsidy, up to 4 yrs)
grants.eligibility: Deep-tech startups in resource circulation or efficient mobility

grants.name: NEDO startup support (DTSU, SBIR Phase 3, NEP)
Startup loans (New Business and Startup Support Fund)
Tokyo startup subsidy (Sogyo Josei)
grants.agency: Tokyo Metropolitan Small and Medium Enterprise Support Center
grants.eligibility: Founders starting a business in Tokyo

grants.name: J-Grants subsidy portal
grants.eligibility: Portal for applying to national subsidies

notes: In Oct 2026 the JETRO website showed a suspension notice after unauthorized access, so some JETRO links may be intermittent. The Business Manager visa capital requirement rose to JPY 30M in Oct 2025, according to the Tokyo startup visa page. For GX_UPP the submission window is 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-17. Web search was exhausted during research, so several entries were verified by site checks only.

summary: Large, heavily state-backed ecosystem centred on Seoul (Gangnam, Pangyo), with the TIPS and KVIC fund-of-funds model at its core. Strong in AI, semiconductors, gaming, beauty and content. Unicorns include Toss, Danggeun and Musinsa, and Coupang listed on NYSE.
startup_visa: D-8-4 Technology Startup visa through the OASIS points program (Ministry of Justice), plus the Startup Korea Special Visa track for founders selected through government programs such as KSGC. https://www.hikorea.go.kr
company_setup: Chusik Hoesa (stock company). Foreign investment is registered through KOTRA / Invest Korea, and KRW 100M or more of investment is needed for the D-8 investor visa. Incorporation takes about 1-3 weeks. Remote setup is possible through an agent with apostilled documents.

grants.name: TIPS (Tech Incubator Program for Startups)
grants.agency: Ministry of SMEs and Startups / KISED
grants.amount: R&D up to KRW 800M over 2 yrs (2026 rules) plus add-ons
grants.eligibility: Startups invested by a TIPS operator (min KRW 200M; KRW 100M outside Seoul region)

grants.name: KOSME startup policy loans (incl. Youth Startup Fund)
grants.amount: low-interest loans, youth fund up to KRW 100M

grants.name: SME technology development (R&D) programs
grants.agency: TIPA / Ministry of SMEs and Startups

accelerators.name: K-Startup Grand Challenge (KSGC)
accelerators.investment: no equity, prize money and grants for top teams, up to KRW 8M travel

accelerators.name: SparkLabs Korea
accelerators.investment: usually KRW 100M+ for about 6% (CPS or SAFE)
accelerators.deadline: windows each April and September (about 1.5 months)

accelerators.name: D.CAMP
accelerators.investment: no equity, investment through D.Day demo days

accelerators.name: Mashup Ventures
accelerators.investment: seed up to about KRW 500M, TIPS operator

accelerators.name: Centers for Creative Economy and Innovation (CCEI)

resources.name: Korea Institute of Startup and Entrepreneurship Development (KISED)

notes: KSGC 2026 ran May 6 to June 17, 2026. The next call (KSGC 2027) is expected around May-June 2027 but is not yet published. The old k-startupgc.org domain now hosts unrelated content, so use ksgc.global. TIPS rules changed in 2026: R&D ceiling KRW 800M and operator minimum KRW 200M, per press reports. Most government calls are published in the K-Startup integrated announcement each January.

summary: Hardware and semiconductor powerhouse with a growing software, AI and deep-tech startup scene centred on Taipei, Hsinchu and Kaohsiung. The government brand Startup Island TAIWAN and the National Development Fund co-invest heavily. Gogoro and Appier are the best-known exits.
startup_visa: Entrepreneur Visa (MOEA Department of Investment Review) and the Employment Gold Card for qualified professionals, https://goldcard.nat.gov.tw
company_setup: Company limited by shares or limited company. Foreign investment needs prior approval from MOEA's Department of Investment Review and a local agent or address. No general minimum capital, though it must cover costs, and NT$6M is needed if sponsoring an Entrepreneur Visa through the investment route. Takes about 3-6 weeks.

grants.name: SBIR (Small Business Innovation Research)
grants.amount: Phase 1 up to NT$1.5M; Phase 2 up to NT$10M

grants.name: National Development Fund co-investment (incl. Angel Investment Program)
TTA programs (CES and international showcase support)
grants.deadline: per call (TTA x CES 2027 call opened 2026-07-02)

accelerators.name: AppWorks Accelerator
accelerators.investment: free, no equity (AppWorks funds may invest separately)
accelerators.sectors: AI, defense tech, on-chain finance, generalist

accelerators.name: Taiwan Startup Terrace (Linkou and Asia New Bay)
accelerators.deadline: residency reviews several times a year

vcs.name: AppWorks Funds
vcs.sectors: AI, web3, Southeast Asia and Greater China tech

resources.name: Taiwan Employment Gold Card
resources.note: Work and residence permit for talent

notes: The NDF site (df.gov.tw) blocks automated fetches, so program amounts were not confirmed. The Taiwan Startup Stadium homepage looked partly outdated in Oct 2026. The Department of Investment Review site could not be reached from the research environment. Web search was exhausted during research.

summary: International finance hub with a startup scene focused on fintech, biotech, AI and Greater Bay Area access, anchored by HKSTP and Cyberport. Government funding has grown sharply through ITF, the HK Investment Corporation and talent schemes. SenseTime, Klook and WeLab are notable names.
startup_visa: Investment as Entrepreneurs (Immigration Department), plus the Top Talent Pass Scheme for high earners and graduates, https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/visas/investment.html
company_setup: Private company limited by shares. Online incorporation with the Companies Registry, no residency requirement but a local company secretary and address are needed. Takes about 1-5 days and costs about HK$1,500-2,000 in fees. Profits tax is 8.25% on the first HK$2M.

grants.name: Enterprise Support Scheme (ESS)
grants.amount: up to HK$10M per project, 1:1 matching

grants.name: Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU)
grants.eligibility: Spin-offs of 6 HK universities (TSSSU-O up to 2 yrs, TSSSU+ up to 7 yrs)

grants.name: RAISe+ Scheme
grants.amount: up to HK$100M per project, matching

grants.name: Innovation and Technology Venture Fund (ITVF)
grants.amount: co-investment at about 1:2 with partner VCs
grants.eligibility: Local I&T startups backed by co-investment partners

grants.name: SME Export Marketing Fund and BUD Fund

accelerators.name: HKSTP Incubation Programme (Incu-Tech, Incu-Bio)
accelerators.investment: no equity, funding support and space

resources.name: InvestHK
resources.note: Free setup support for foreign firms

resources.name: Hong Kong Venture Capital and Private Equity Association

notes: As of Oct 2026 the Technology Voucher Programme (TVP) is not listed on the ITF programme index and its old ITF page returns 404. Its current status could not be confirmed, so it is left out. hkstp.org timed out and cyberport.hk blocked automated fetches during research, so incubation funding amounts and intake dates were not confirmed.

summary: Small, government-led ecosystem built around youth entrepreneurship, diversification beyond gaming, and the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin. Support is mostly interest-free loans, incubation space and Greater Bay Area programs.
startup_visa: none (no startup visa; non-residents typically enter via investment or talent schemes)
company_setup: Sociedade por quotas (limited company), minimum capital MOP25,000. Registered through the Commercial and Movable Property Registry, with help from IPIM's Investor One Stop Service. Takes about 1-3 weeks.

grants.name: Young Entrepreneurs Aid Scheme
grants.amount: interest-free loan up to MOP300,000, repaid over up to 10 yrs
grants.eligibility: Macao resident young entrepreneurs or companies over 50% owned by them

grants.name: Science and Technology Development Fund funding

resources.name: IPIM: Macao Trade and Investment Promotion Institute
Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin

notes: No Macau-based VC with a verifiable official site was found. Founders usually raise from Hong Kong or Mainland funds. Many Hengqin youth-entrepreneurship programs are listed on Mainland sites that could not be verified.

summary: Small ecosystem centred on Ulaanbaatar, strongest in fintech, e-commerce and govtech (e-Mongolia). The Mongolian Startup Association runs community events, and the first local VC funds are only forming. Capital mostly comes from banks, conglomerates and development finance institutions.
company_setup: LLC registered with the General Authority for State Registration. Foreign-invested companies generally need foreign equity of at least about US$100k to register as such, so smaller foreign founders often use local partners. Takes about 2-4 weeks.

grants.name: SME Agency concessional loans (SME Development Fund)

vcs.name: ADB Ventures
vcs.sectors: climate, inclusion tech in ADB member countries

vcs.name: EBRD (venture and small business programs)
vcs.sectors: SMEs and growth firms in EBRD countries incl. Mongolia

notes: No Mongolia-based VC or accelerator with a current, verifiable official site was confirmed. The Mongolian Startup Association site mentions the first local VC fund forming in 2025. The SME Agency site lists loan intake but no published terms.

summary: No accessible private startup ecosystem. The economy is state-controlled and under comprehensive UN, US and EU sanctions, so foreign investment, payments and tech transfer are effectively prohibited.
company_setup: Not possible for foreign founders under current sanctions. Private enterprise is not legally recognised.
notes: Sanctions as of Oct 2026: any investment or business is effectively prohibited. Listed for completeness only.
